_readme: Public DFIR research images we can validate against. Committed so a fresh
session knows what exists without re-researching it, and so 'we tested against
a real device' names WHICH device.
Every entry is a full-filesystem image that ALSO contains an iTunes/Finder
backup. Only the backup half is kept locally: it is what this app reads, it is
~2 GB against ~22 GB for the archive, and disk is the binding constraint (see
scripts/fetch-test-image.sh, which deletes the archive once the backup is out).
SOURCE AND TERMS: Josh Hickman's research images, hosted by Digital Corpora,
which states its images 'are freely available and may be used without prior
`backup_password` is the password Hickman sets on the backup and publishes in
the accompanying documentation. It is not a secret and it protects nothing —
`have` is not recorded here: what is on disk is what is on disk, and a flag in
a committed file would go stale the moment someone prunes. Ask the script.

images.notes: The image every parser and module in the repo is currently validated against. «redacted» manifest entries, 57 third-party apps.

Fetched. `ios`/`device` are read from the fetched backup's Info.plist, not from the upstream description, which says iPhone 12 / 16.5 — what is on disk is an iPhone 11 (serial F4GZ987AN72N) at 16.1.2, the SAME physical device as ios17 one OS earlier. That makes it the ideal drift check: same data, different iOS. The password was recorded as null and is not; it decrypts with the same one as ios17, which is why every module 'failed' against it in corpus mode.

DIRECT ENCRYPTED-BACKUP DOWNLOAD, not a full-filesystem image: a 474 MB zip of the iTunes backup itself, so no tar/FFS step and nothing to prune. iPhone 8 at 15.3.1 (serial FFMW4BH5JC67), a DIFFERENT physical device from the iPhone 11 (ios16/ios17) and the iPhone SE (ios13/ios13_4) — the corpus's only iOS 15 and its only iPhone 8. Lives under the Digital Corpora `android_13/ios_15_3_1/` prefix, which is why the old iOS15/ guess 404'd. Password `MyBackup123` (note: NOT `MyPassword123` like ios16/ios17) is documented on the last page of iOS15-ImageCreation.pdf. `backup_zip: true` tells fetch-test-image.sh the url is the backup zip directly.

The URL recorded here was wrong (iOS13/iOS_13_Public_Image.tar.gz, 404); the real path is ios_13_3_1/ios_13_3_1.zip. 8.93 GB, but THE BACKUP INSIDE IS 396 MB -- a single zip member. tools/fetch-zip-member.py range-fetches just that, so this costs 4% of the archive. Oldest lineage available, and the one that exercises every older-schema SQL alternative the modules carry. PASSWORD IS LOWERCASE -- `mypassword123`, not the `MyPassword123` that opens ios16 and ios17. It is in the image-creation PDF, not in image_info.txt, which reports 'Password Protected: false' while the Manifest says IsEncrypted: true. A DIFFERENT PHYSICAL DEVICE too (iPhone SE, serial DX3T126VH2XV) rather than the iPhone 11 of the other two.

The SAME iPhone SE as ios13 (serial DX3T126VH2XV), one point release later. A point-release pair is weaker than a major-version one for schema drift -- kept because the backup member is 420 MB via tools/fetch-zip-member.py, which is cheap enough that a fourth device-state costs less than deciding whether to want it.
